verdict.rationale: Sentry documents some background automation: Seer "automatically root-cause[s] any issue" and can hand its analysis to a connected coding agent for automated fix generation and pull-request creation. Alerts, webhooks and AI code review also provide event-driven automation. However, the evidence shows no general way for users to define and schedule their own autonomous automations. Much of the support rests on page titles, and Seer requires a paid subscription. Missing for 10: a documented user-configurable automation/workflow builder, details of how Seer autofix triggers run unattended, depth beyond feature titles for alerts and webhooks, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
